Expected packets worked out from OpenRGB's C++ (commit d4798c120659ec5ba2e664a9e87bedff8d36f880, Controllers/WootingKeyboardController) by a separate reference model that mirrors each C++ function buffer by buffer (openrgb-work/batch2/hyperx/gen_fixtures.py in the porting session's scratch space, not part of the repository); plugin.js was never run to make them. 'products' comes from the detector file (WootingKeyboardControllerDetect.cpp; the _WIN32 branch where there is one). Each variant lists the exposed LEDs (name, OpenRGB LED index, grid cell), two colour sets in that order, the I/O for Initialize, a frame with each colour set and Shutdown, and how long an unchanged frame may go unsent (resend_ms, 0 = every Render). ops: write = output report (hid_write), send_report = feature report (hid_send_feature_report), pause = sleep; hex is the whole buffer at the length the C++ passes, report id first. Lightloom deviations described in docs/hardware/wooting.md are modelled the same way (Shutdown sends the RESET_ALL colour command (0x20) instead of nothing).
